source_review.notes: Checked all 13 structured references against current official Apache Iceberg, Delta Lake, and Apache Hudi specifications/documentation. Verified rewrite-data-files strategies and metrics, streaming small-file guidance, optimistic concurrency, bin packing, optimized/automatic writes, no-data-change hazards, merge-on-read compaction, log compaction, clustering distinctions, file sizing, timeline replacement, and retention/cleanup behavior in their stated scopes; all final URLs returned HTTP 200.

evidence: Checked definitions for snapshot-visible multisets, input/output file sets, deletes/logs, rewrite groups, file-size fractions, output estimates, amplification, planning cost, priority, and break-even.
Checked every displayed fraction, ceiling, set transition, equality, cost, and scheduling expression for defined terms and balanced syntax.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation consistently distinguishes physical files and byte sizing from logical visible rows, atomic snapshot transitions, economic estimates, and lifecycle reachability.

evidence: Executed small-file-bin-packing and matched five inputs, 170 input units, groups (70,30) and (40,20,10), output sizes 100 and 70, and file reduction three.
Recomputed visible rows before and after applying deleted key b and confirmed identical five-row key/value multisets with the deleted key absent.
Checked the example file-rate arithmetic: 24 partitions times 1,440 minute commits equals 34,560 files per day under the one-file-per-partition-per-commit simplification.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All concrete values and executable outputs were independently recomputed; byte targets and economic examples remain explicitly workload-specific.

evidence: Verified that atomic replacement preserves the full visible table multiset when selected input visibility equals output visibility and all outside files are unchanged.
Verified count and byte small-file fractions have different denominators and diagnose control-plane burden versus rewrite scope.
Verified output-count, amplification, planning-cost, priority, and break-even expressions are scoped as estimates or measured models rather than correctness proofs.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The chapter correctly separates logical equivalence, physical packing, operational benefit, and cleanup reachability.

evidence: Reviewed empty and oversized records, variable row widths, compression changes, skewed partitions/tasks, tiny tails, overlarge files, hot/late partitions, changing schemas/specs, and grouping restrictions.

Reviewed position/equality deletes, deletion vectors, merge logs, sequence applicability, no-data-change markers, stale inputs, retries, speculative candidates, partial progress, commit limits, and overlapping writers.
Reviewed old snapshots, active readers/streams, branches/tags/holds, orphan races, temporary double storage, encryption, privacy erasure, capacity starvation, and regressions in data skipping.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Adversarial cases cover silent row resurrection, stale replacement, partial visibility, metadata corruption, historical breakage, performance regression, and uneconomic maintenance.

evidence: Traced pinned input identity, isolated candidate creation, exact-input conflict validation, atomic replacement, and old-file retention through the overview, exposition, proof, examples, and answers.
Confirmed visible row/key multiplicity, schema/partition/spec/statistics/encryption, delete/log/sequence, and change-feed semantics are preserved independently of file count.
Confirmed prevention, sizing, economics, capacity, partial-progress accounting, cleanup reachability, observability, and ownership remain separate required gates.
invariant_checking.notes: No target size, file reduction, flag, successful output write, or current-snapshot absence is treated as sufficient proof of a correct and valuable compaction.

evidence: Reviewed the eight-step atomic compaction transparency proof from pinned inputs and visible semantics through candidate equivalence, conflict validation, atomic publication, and historical retention.
Checked that partial progress composes only when each committed rewrite group independently meets the same relation-preservation premises.
proof_review.notes: The proof is valid under its stated table-format schema, partition, delete/log, sequence, conflict, and atomic-publication assumptions.

evidence: The atomic transparency argument is explicitly labeled a proof sketch.
The following paragraph excludes performance benefit, bitwise identity, row order, and implementations that bypass delete/sequence rules.
Packing and economic formulas are labeled estimates, heuristics, indicators, or measured models.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No vendor behavior, threshold, sample benchmark, or cost estimate is mislabeled as a universal theorem.

evidence: Current product behaviors are attributed to dated primary specifications/documentation and remain scoped to the named format or engine.
The executable explicitly disclaims implementation of Iceberg, Delta Lake, Hudi, Parquet, delete files, object stores, and distributed writers.
The chapter distinguishes file bin packing, merge/log compaction, manifest/log compaction, and clustering rather than generalizing one product's terminology.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Specification guarantees, teaching abstractions, operational observations, and organization-specific thresholds are clearly distinguished.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed the chapter end to end. It explains small-file causes and fixed costs, then develops workload-specific sizing, eligibility, packing, delete-aware atomic rewrite, concurrency, partial progress, prevention, economics, validation, cleanup, and ownership without conflating compaction categories.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed the retrieval inventory, compaction contract, lower/target/upper bands, plan identity, conflict-safe retries, writer prevention, maintenance scheduling, cost model, validation controls, cleanup horizons, dashboards, alerts, and runbook responsibilities for production implementability.

pedagogical_review.notes: Reviewed progression from one-page definitions through diagnosis, equations, proof sketch, executable first-fit-decreasing model, trade-offs, 26 misconceptions, ten examples, cross-program connections, and five distinct exercises with worked answers. Connections accurately build from DE-034/036/055/063–066 into DE-068–070.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
